title: Annual hidden low-runoff states in 554 US reference basins (WY1951-2016) occurred at the rate of stationary simulations, did not follow dry years, and mostly ended in WY2017-2025
abstract: Question: Peterson et al. (2021) found that many Victorian catchments changed to a persistent low-runoff state during the Millennium Drought. Does this occur in the contiguous United States? Approach: we used 554 CAMELS-US reference basins with USGS daily flow and nClimGrid basin precipitation for water years (WY) 1951-2025. We fitted the annual two-state hidden Markov model form of hydroState (Box-Cox runoff linear in rainfall, states change the intercept and error sd, AIC selection) to WY1951-2016 and tested WY2017-2025 out of sample. We calibrated the detection with synthetic series from stationary 1-state models, with and without previous-year rainfall (3 replicates each). Results: AIC chose a 2-state model in 73% of real basins and in 72-76% of stationary synthetic series. The shift rule flagged 23.3% of real basins (95% CI 19.9-26.7%) and 13.5-18.4% of synthetic series. A post hoc mean-shift form (one shared error sd) flagged 11.2% of real basins versus 8.7-13.0% of synthetic series (expected 56, observed 62, P = 0.17). Low-state onsets did not follow dry periods (3-year precipitation z +0.06; null -0.15 to +0.15). Of 54 basins in the low state in WY2016, 42 returned to the normal state in WY2017-2025; 10 of the 12 others are eastern basins with one long low block that started in 1985-2006. Where AIC chose a 2-state model, it predicted WY2017-2025 runoff worse than the best 1-state model (median -0.087 log units per year, CI -0.106 to -0.068). California runoff fell below its rainfall relation in 2012-2016 (-0.34 SD) and was at or above it in 2017-2025 (+0.21 SD, CI -0.04 to +0.46). Conclusion: at the annual scale, US reference basins show no clear excess of hidden low-runoff states over stationary series and no Victorian-type non-recovery after the 2012-2016 drought. An AIC preference for a 2-state annual runoff model is not evidence of a state change without matched null simulations. Limitations: annual model only; our Python port of the model form, not the hydroState package; Gaussian synthetic errors; possible gauge, land-use and grid-network effects in the eastern low blocks; WY2026 provisional data not interpreted; mean-shift and memory tests were added after interim results.

citations.reason: Reuses its Python port of the hydroState annual model (hmm.py) and compares the US result with its Victorian 2018-2025 result.
